newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's top soldier wasn't consulted on tunnel.
newsitem.headline: Israel's top soldier wasn't consulted on tunnel.

text.p: Israel's top soldier said on Friday that the army had only several hours notice on the opening of a tunnel in Jerusalem that sparked bloody clashes between Israelis and Palestinians this week.
"We only knew about its opening on the evening after Yom Kippur," Army Chief of Staff Lieutenant-General Amnon Shahak told Israel Radio.

Israel punched a second entrance into an archaeological tunnel running near Islamic holy places in Jerusalem's Old City in the pre-dawn hours of Tuesday. Yom Kippur, the Jewish Day of Atonement, ended on Monday evening.

Shahak said the army was not usually included in consultations about Jerusalem. His statement came a day after Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said perhaps not all factors were taken into account when the decision was made.

Israeli military commentator Zeev Schiff wrote in Israel's Haaretz newspaper on Thursday that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu did not hold thorough security consultations before making the controversial move.

"Not all heads of security organs -- those involved in the affairs of the territories and Palestinians -- were asked their opinions whether it was desirable now to open the tunnel...It is incorrect that the Shin Bet (security force) gave its explicit approval," Schiff wrote.
